aiItems.content:
What is a cherry blossom painting?

A cherry blossom painting is a piece of artwork that depicts the flowering branches of the cherry blossom tree — known in Japan as sakura — and is one of the most enduring motifs in Asian art and culture. These paintings traditionally use ink wash or watercolour techniques to capture the delicate, fleeting beauty of blossom blooms, often set against soft or minimal backgrounds in keeping with Japanese artistic values. In contemporary home decor, cherry blossom paintings are popular for their calming, nature-inspired quality and their versatility — they suit Japandi, minimalist and Asian-inspired interiors especially well. A set of wall art prints featuring cherry blossom scenes is a simple, impactful way to bring that sense of quiet beauty into a bedroom or living space.

How to Hang a Cherry Blossom Painting Set of 3 in a Bedroom

1. Choose your wall: Pick a wall with enough horizontal space for all three prints side by side — above the bed's headboard is the most popular spot, as it creates a natural focal point in the room.

2. Measure and mark: Lay the three prints on the floor first to work out your preferred spacing — a gap of 5 to 8 cm between each print usually looks balanced. Mark the hanging points on the wall with a pencil before putting in any fixings.

3. Hang at eye level: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level when you're standing — for most bedrooms that's around 145 to 155 cm from the floor to the middle of each print. If hanging above a headboard, aim for the bottom of the prints to sit about 15 to 20 cm above the top of the headboard.

4. Check alignment: Use a spirit level across all three prints once they're up — even a slight tilt is really noticeable with a set. Step back and look from the doorway to get the full effect.

5. Style around the prints: Keep the surrounding decor simple to let the Japandi ink artwork breathe — natural textures, neutral bedding and minimal clutter on bedside tables will let the set do the work.

Choosing Your Cherry Blossom Wall Art Print Format

Unframed Print — The print only, ready for you to frame in your own choice of frame. Available on Luster art paper (vibrant, semi-sheen finish) or Museum quality paper (ultra-fine detail, archival standard). Great if you already have a frame or want to match your own decor exactly.

Framed Print — Your chosen print is mounted and framed, arriving completely ready to hang — no sourcing a frame, no hassle. Available in multiple sizes on Luster or Museum quality paper. The most convenient option if you want the set on your wall with minimal effort.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped around a wooden stretcher frame — no glazing, no frame needed. Has a natural texture that suits the ink-brush style of this Japandi set particularly well. Simply hang straight onto the wall. Available in a range of canvas sizes.

Paper quality: Luster vs Museum — Luster art paper gives a semi-gloss, vibrant finish that makes the black ink and red blossom tones pop. Museum quality paper is the premium archival choice — it captures every fine detail in the brushwork and is made to last for decades without fading. Both are printed with fade-resistant pigment inks in the UK.

What is London Artwork?

London artwork refers to art prints, paintings or illustrations that feature iconic London landmarks, cityscapes or urban scenes — such as Big Ben, the Shard, the Thames or the wider city skyline. It is a broad and popular category that covers everything from photographic prints to hand-drawn illustrations and painterly watercolour styles. London artwork is especially popular for bedrooms, living rooms and home offices, where it adds a sense of personality and a connection to one of the world's most recognisable cities. As a subject it suits contemporary, industrial and travel-inspired interior styles particularly well, and a set of three coordinating prints is a great way to create a real focal point on any wall.

How to Hang London Artwork as a Set of 3

1. Plan your layout first: Lay all three prints on the floor or a bed in the order you want to hang them. For a horizontal triptych like this London skyline set, line them up left to right so the cityscape flows naturally across all three pieces.

2. Mark your wall: Decide on the overall width the set will take up and find the centre point of that space. Mark it lightly with a pencil. This ensures your set sits symmetrically on the wall rather than drifting to one side.

3. Set your height: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level — around 145–150 cm from the floor is a good guide for most rooms. If you are hanging above a bed or sofa, aim for the bottom of the prints to sit about 20–25 cm above the furniture.

4. Space the prints evenly: A gap of 5–8 cm between each print tends to look intentional and balanced. Use a ruler or a strip of card as a spacer so every gap is identical.

5. Hang and step back: Once all three are up, step back and look from a distance. Small adjustments at this stage are much easier than you think — and the result is always worth taking a moment to get right.

Choosing Your London Artwork Format: Which Option is Right for You?

Unframed Print — The print is delivered on its own, ready for you to frame in a style of your choosing. Great if you already have a frame in mind or want to match existing decor precisely. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Your art print arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to a frame shop needed. A brilliant time-saving option and ideal as a gift. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper in multiple sizes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, giving a gallery-style finish with no glass. The image wraps slightly around the edges for a clean, contemporary look. Arrives ready to hang.

Luster Paper (print options) — A semi-gloss surface that gives colours and contrasts a little extra punch — works especially well with the moody dark tones in this London skyline set.

Museum Quality Paper (print options) — A fine-art matte surface that complements the painterly, watercolour character of this artwork. A softer, more gallery-like feel.

What is an abstract artwork painting?

An abstract artwork painting is a piece — or set of pieces — where the artist interprets a subject through expressive colour, loose form and painterly mark-making rather than strict realism, giving you the feeling and atmosphere of a place or idea rather than a photographic record of it. In the context of wall art prints, this means you get all the visual energy and character of a hand-painted artwork reproduced at high quality so it can be enjoyed in your home. Abstract city and travel paintings like this Paris skyline set blend recognisable landmarks — the Eiffel Tower, grand domed architecture, soaring skyscrapers — with fluid brushstrokes, layered tones and expressive skies to create something that feels both familiar and genuinely artistic. They work particularly well in contemporary bedrooms because the loose, painterly quality adds warmth and texture that photography-based prints sometimes lack. As art prints, they offer all of this at an accessible price point, with the option to choose your preferred finish and framing.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Abstract Artwork Painting Prints in Your Bedroom

1. Measure your wall space first: Hold a tape measure across the area where you plan to hang the prints — above a bed headboard is ideal. Write down the total width available, then divide by three and subtract your preferred gap (4–6 cm between each print is a tidy, contemporary spacing).

2. Mark your hanging points in pencil: Use a spirit level to draw a faint horizontal pencil line at your desired hanging height — roughly 150–160 cm from the floor to the centre of the prints is a comfortable eye-level position. Mark the centre of the wall first, then measure outward evenly for prints two and three so the set sits symmetrically.

3. Use two fixings per print: A single nail can allow prints to tilt over time. Two picture hooks or wall fixings per print, spaced evenly inside the frame width, keep everything straight and secure — especially important with the larger size options.

4. Step back and adjust before committing: Once the first print is up, hold the remaining two in position (a second pair of hands helps enormously here) and check the spacing looks even from across the room rather than up close — our eyes judge art from a distance, not from a centimetre away.

5. Check the level one final time: Run your spirit level across all three prints together once they're all hung. Even a 1–2 mm tilt is visible in a set of three, so it's worth the extra thirty seconds to get it spot on.

Which Option Is Right for You? Comparing Print and Canvas Choices

Unframed Print on Luster Paper — A great-value option if you already have frames at home or want to choose your own. Luster paper gives a gentle sheen that makes the grey and beige tones in this Paris skyline set feel lively and rich. You will need to source your own frames.

Unframed Print on Museum Quality Paper — The finest print finish we offer — exceptional colour accuracy and depth, making the deep charcoal and maroon shadow tones in this artwork really sing. Ideal if you are a print collector or want the very best reproduction. Again, framing is down to you.

Framed Print (Luster or Museum Quality) — Arrives completely ready to hang straight out of the box — no frame hunting, no guesswork. A real time-saver and the most popular choice for bedroom wall art. Simply choose your paper quality at checkout and hang on the day it arrives.

Wrapped Canvas — A gallery-style option where the print wraps around a deep wooden stretcher frame — no additional framing needed at all. The image extends around the edges for a clean, contemporary look that suits modern and urban-styled bedrooms perfectly. Ready to hang immediately.
